data.name: Manasvin
data.gender_notes: Manasvin is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Manasvin is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Manas' which means 'mind' and 'Vin' which means 'god'. The name Manasvin carries the meaning “God of mind” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Manasvin usually hope their child will grow to embody god of mind and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents the divine mind and intellect.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Manasvin total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

historical_references.reference: Manasvin is a name mentioned in the ancient Hindu text 'Rigveda'. It is the name of a horse sacrifice offered by the mythological king Divodasa to Indra, the god of thunder, rain, and storms.
Manasvin is also a name of a celestial river mentioned in the Hindu epic 'Mahabharata'. The river flows between the mountains Meru and Mandara, and is believed to be the source of the Ganges River.
